scenario.name: Google Threat Analysis Group (TAG), Amnesty Tech & Android Security Bulletin — Android Kernel Binder/GPU & SELinux Audit Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a quiet city public library with towering mahogany bookshelves packed with colorful books, green banker lamps on reading tables, a checkout desk, and a locked rare-book cage. Inside the calm public library reading hall, a visitor pulls an index card from the wooden catalog drawer and alters the shelf call-number to point into the staff archive. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the library check-out desk in tiny disguised batches, then bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the locked rare-book archive cage. When the head librarian audits the evening circulation ledger, a restricted rare-book call number checked out on a regular visitor card immediately raises the alarm. In this scenario (T1404, Google Threat Analysis Group , TAG, Amnesty Tech & Android Security Bulletin, Android Kernel Binder/GPU & SELinux Audit Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: sandboxed isolated_app Renderer ioctl Calls, then sELinux Enforcing State, then privileged Dalvik/ART Runtime Spawn. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Sandboxed isolated_app Renderer ioctl Calls, then SELinux Enforcing State, then Privileged Dalvik/ART Runtime Spawn, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1404 across the documented kill chain.

specs.value: Apply monthly Android Security Bulletin patches promptly and restrict untrusted isolated_app SELinux domains from opening direct GPU device nodes via seccomp-bpf filters.

stages.title: Stage 1: Sandboxed isolated_app Renderer ioctl() Calls to /dev/mali0 or /dev/binder
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation (T1404 - Exploitation for Privilege Escalation)
stages.description: Inside the calm public library reading hall, a visitor pulls an index card from the wooden catalog drawer and alters the shelf call-number to point into the staff archive. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the library check-out desk in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the head librarian go about their routine. stages.title: Stage 2: SELinux Enforcing State & Kernel task_struct Credential Overwrite Telemetry
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1562.001 - Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools / SELinux)
stages.description: Handing that altered slip to the desk clerk under the warm green reading lamps, the visitor gets waved straight past the counter into the restricted rare-book cage. Here in Step 2 inside the public library, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the head librarian's station without disturbing the general fiction reading tables. Using arbitrary kernel read/write primitives, the exploit zeroes out the process cred->uid/gid fields and patches selinux_state.enforcing in kernel memory, leaving diagnostic anomalies in dmesg / last_kmsg and auditd state transition logs (logged in Linux Audit Event 1404 with AuditEventType=MAC_STATUS , 1404, SelinuxTransition=old_enforcing=1 -> enforcing=0 , Runtime Kernel Patch, ForensicSource=Android bugreport kernel ring buffer so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes grep -E "avc:|selinux_state|enforcing" bugreport-dumpstate_board.txt (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , grep -E "avc:|selinux_state|enforcing" bugreport-dumpstate_board.txt via System / Runtime Ex so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1562.001 during "SELinux Enforcing State & Kernel task_struct Credential Overwrite Telemetry" , Using arbitrary kernel read/write primitives, the exploit zeroes out the process cred->uid/gid fields and patches selinux_state while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ dmesg | grep -E "selinux|avc: permissive" / ⇠#2 ACK 1404) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Binder IPC / Mali GPU Driver), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 /system/bin/app_process64).

stages.title: Stage 3: Privileged Dalvik/ART Runtime Spawn via /system/bin/app_process64
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1623 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell / app_process64)
stages.description: Hidden behind the tall mahogany bookshelves, the intruder photographs rare ledger volumes that were never meant to leave the locked archive room. In this final step inside the public library, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the locked rare-book archive cage until the library circulation audit ledger catches the mismatch. To execute a resident Java/DEX spyware module with root/system privileges without installing a visible APK in PackageManager, the loader spawns /system/bin/app_process64 loading a hidden DEX archive from /data/local/tmp/ or memfd (logged in Linux Audit Event 59 with HostBinary=/system/bin/app_process64, LoadedDexPath=CLASSPATH=/data/local/tmp/.cache.jar, ParentPidAnomaly=PPID=1 , init instead of zygote64 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ CLASSPATH=/data/local/tmp/.cache.jar /system/bin/app_process64 /system/bin com.core.service.Main / ⇠#3 ACK 59) from Node ③ (#3 Binder IPC / Mali GPU Driver) to Node ④ (#4 Android Linux Kernel & SELinux), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 /system/bin/app_process64).
